newsitem.title: USA: Invacare says Healthdyne offer expires.
newsitem.headline: Invacare says Healthdyne offer expires.

text.p: Invacare Corp on Friday confirmed that the $15 all-cash tender offer by its subsidiary for Healthdyne Technologies Inc has expired without any shares being purchased.
Invacare, which had launched a $200 million hostile bid for Healthdyne, said the depositary will return all shares tendered in the offer and not withdrawn.
Healthdyne management engaged in a six-month fight for control of the company. And on Wednesday, shareholders re-elected its slate of directors, rejecting a dissident slate offered by Invacare.

Invacare Chairman and Chief Executive Malachi Mixon said in a statement that based on the proxies the company had received, it appeared that Healthdyne's board was elected, and "there is no point in continuing our tender offer at this time."

"We continue to be interested in acquiring Healthdyne, but we cannot wait around idly," he added. "Therefore, we intend to pursue alternative steps necessary to establish a strong position for Invacare in the sleep apnea market."
